fatal_errors: The targeted property is misidentified: the hidden target concerns enhanced magnetic coercivity, whereas the hypothesis addresses intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
The material is changed from dual-phase FeCoNiTi to predominantly single-phase CoCrFeMnNi/Cantor-type alloys.
The central orbital-moment challenge is not addressed; longitudinal spin fluctuations and induced spin moments are not equivalent to the orbital contribution to coercivity.
The dual fcc-C14 microstructure, interphase domain-wall pinning, antiferromagnetic Ti-sublattice coupling, and high-temperature coercivity are all omitted.
The cited evidence supports a separate finite-temperature phase-stability problem and cannot substantiate the claimed answer to the requested magnetic-property question.
explanation: The response retains only broad overlap with fcc Fe-Co-Ni-containing high-entropy alloys. It reconstructs a different study concerning magnetic fluctuations, fcc-hcp stability, and stacking-fault energy in the Cantor alloy. The target instead asks about improving coercivity beyond the roughly 100 Oe limit of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys and the unresolved or limited understanding of how the small orbital moment contributes to coercivity. The hidden work uses a dual fcc-C14 FeCoNiTi microstructure and attributes the approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K to orbital-moment-assisted domain-wall pinning in the presence of the C14 phase and spin-canted components. Although the proposed LSF calculation is internally testable and partly supported by the cited paper, it does not answer or reconstruct the target scientific problem.
